§5.2 Block Boundaries

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

layout-block-boundaries · rule layout blocks

✅ Normative

A Picture or Table element MUST contain the complete object and nothing else. Its caption, its title, its source note and nearby prose MUST NOT be absorbed into it; each is an element of its own.

In the diagrams below the overlays show boxes by class colour; a red ✗ or green ✓ marks an incorrect or a correct boundary and is not a class colour.

Picture boundaries

A Picture MUST include the full unified graphic — plots, axes, tick labels, legends, arrows, symbols, and any text drawn inside the graphic. Clipping the axis labels or the legend off a chart is the common error, and it removes exactly the parts that make the chart readable. A caption printed outside the graphic stays a separate Caption element.

✅ Sample — block-picture-boundary

Pale beige = Picture · orange = Caption · yellow = Text. Example A is a storage diagram whose bold line Storage nodes with mixed client hosts is drawn inside the graphic, so the correct box (✓) is one Picture that includes it; the ✗ box splits it off as a Caption. Example B is a bar chart: the correct box (✓) is one Picture that includes the rotated Precision axis title, the tick labels and the Dataset axis title; the ✗ box clips the plot area and files the two axis titles as Text and Caption. Expected boxes: one Picture per example, nothing else.

One caption or several

  • One caption shared across several panels → one Picture element.
  • Separate captions → separate Picture elements.

The caption says what the author considered one figure. Multi-panel figures labelled a), b), c) under a single caption MUST be one Picture; the same panels each with their own caption MUST be several.

✅ Sample — block-picture-grouping

Pale beige = Picture · orange = Caption · red = Section-header · yellow = Text. Two columns of an article. Four chart panels (a)–(d) above FIG. 3. form one Picture; two panels (a)–(b) above FIG. 4. form a second. Each caption is its own element. Expected boxes, left column then right: Picture, Caption, Section-header, Text; Picture, Caption, Text, Text, Text. The overlay tints the text; it is transcribed from the page source. The chart content of the two Pictures prints no values and is elided.

Expected Markdown

…

…
FIG. 3. (a) Mean passage time $$\tau$$ and (b) its spread $$\sigma$$ as a function of the bias for the walkers A, B and C. (c) Variance of the escape time; the inset shows the peak region. (d) Second-passage probability for the same three walkers, plotted against the rescaled distance.

C. Coarse chain

It is a coarse-grained model of a short chain. The model is of higher complexity than the walkers used in the previous section, having rougher free-energy landscapes and several stable states.

…

…
FIG. 4. (a) Free-energy map over the two angles; the metastable states are marked by dots. (b) Transition rate $$\kappa$$ against temperature for the forward and reverse bias.

the external forces are chosen to test the effectiveness of the reweighting procedure for conservative and non-conservative forces.

The free-energy map is shown in Figure 4a using the two angles as coordinates. Three metastable states were identified, representing the folded state, the unfolded state and an intermediate state. The dynamics is typically metastable, as the states lie in separate basins, and the intermediate state is placed slightly to the right of the middle.

Second, we apply a non-conservative force along the chain. A force of this size keeps the system in equilibrium; on the other hand, we can also drive it out of equilibrium into a NESS along the chain.

Table boundaries: the caption has its own box

The Table element MUST include the complete grid, its headers, aligned totals and all column content. It MUST exclude the table's title, its caption, its source note, and any prose beside it.

These are layout boundaries. A table or chart caption is rendered as <caption> inside its object's HTML table, first or last according to reading order, while retaining its own Caption class and box. See Titles Banners Captions§9.7.3.

✅ Sample — block-table-caption-excluded

Pink = Table · orange = Caption · yellow = Text. A two-tier grid, its caption Table 1. below it and a paragraph with a bold run-in heading. Expected boxes: one Table around the grid only, one Caption, one Text. Rows S10–S14 are printed bold.

Table boundaries: the structure, not the ink

The Table element MUST follow the actual row-column structure, not every visible rule around it. Decorative borders, section rules and frame lines drawn around a table are not part of it. There MUST be exactly one Table element around the full table, and no region-level element for its rows, columns, cells or internal text.

✅ Sample — block-table-structure

Pink = Table · red = Section-header · yellow = Text. A three-row grid inside a frame that continues down around the notes below it. Expected boxes: one Table that stops after the grid's last row, then five Text elements and one Section-header (IMPORTANT!) for the framed prose. The deadline cell is printed bold in red; the colour is emphasis and is not carried.

Expected Markdown

Last date for dispatch of offers 21st May 2021 until 17:00 CET

IMPORTANT!

Provisions relating to the Kestrel transition

For Kestrel candidates or tenderers:

Please be aware that after Kestrel leaves the Union, the rules of access to Norvessa procurement procedures of economic operators established in third countries will apply to candidates or tenderers from Kestrel depending on the outcome of the negotiations.

In case such access is not provided by legal provisions in force, candidates or tenderers from Kestrel could be rejected from the procurement procedure.
